vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper authorization mechanism for socket operations based on the opener of a socket in the Netlink implementation.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: Local users can bypass intended access restrictions and modify network configurations by using a Netlink socket for the stdout or stderr of a setuid program.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to ensure that socket operations are properly authorized based on the capabilities associated with the Netlink socket itself.

added: Add a check using netlink_capable(skb, CAP_NET_ADMIN) to authorize socket operations based on the capabilities of the Netlink socket.
deleted: Remove the existing check using capable(CAP_NET_ADMIN) as it is not sufficient to prevent unauthorized access to network configurations.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper handling for the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: When unsharing a user namespace, the code does not set the CLONE_FS flag along with the CLONE_NEWUSER flag, leading to a vulnerability.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code does not include the CLONE_FS flag when unsharing a user namespace, allowing local users to gain privileges by calling chroot and exploiting the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to ensure that when unsharing a user namespace (CLONE_NEWUSER flag is set), both the CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_FS flags are also set. This prevents local users from gaining privileges by leveraging the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes. The solution involves adding the line 'unshare_flags |= CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_FS;' to properly handle the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.

vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: Setting the cpuctx->ctx.type field to cpu_context without proper validation or sanitization, allowing potential privilege escalation or security issues.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to remove the line that sets cpuctx->ctx.type = cpu_context in the perf_pmu_register function. This prevents local users from gaining privileges via a crafted application by eliminating the potential for unauthorized access or control over system resources through the mishandling of counter grouping.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper handling for the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: When unsharing a user namespace, the code does not set the CLONE_FS flag along with the CLONE_NEWUSER flag, leading to a vulnerability.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code does not include the CLONE_FS flag when unsharing a user namespace, allowing local users to gain privileges by calling chroot and exploiting the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes.

non_vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to ensure that when unsharing a user namespace (CLONE_NEWUSER flag is set), both the CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_FS flags are also set. This prevents local users from gaining privileges by leveraging the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes. The solution involves adding the line 'unshare_flags |= CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_FS;' to properly handle the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper handling for the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: When unsharing a user namespace, the code does not set the CLONE_FS flag along with the CLONE_NEWUSER flag, leading to a vulnerability.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code does not include the CLONE_FS flag when unsharing a user namespace, allowing local users to gain privileges by calling chroot and exploiting the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to ensure that when unsharing a user namespace (CLONE_NEWUSER flag is set), both the CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_FS flags are also set. This prevents local users from gaining privileges by leveraging the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes. The solution involves adding the line 'unshare_flags |= CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_FS;' to properly handle the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to add proper authorization checks based on the capabilities of the socket opener for Netlink socket operations.

deleted: Remove the existing capability checks using the capable function.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Improper context-switching of IOPL on 64-bit PV Xen guests in the Linux kernel.

vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code does not handle the switching of IOPL bits properly during context switches on 64-bit PV Xen guests, allowing local guest OS users to gain privileges, cause a denial of service, or obtain sensitive information by leveraging I/O port access.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to manually switch the IOPL bits in pt_regs->flags during context switches on Xen PV systems. This involves adding a conditional check to compare the IOPL of the previous task with the IOPL of the next task and calling xen_set_iopl_mask to switch the IOPL manually if they differ. By ensuring proper handling of IOPL during context switches, unauthorized privilege escalation, denial of service attacks, and information disclosure through I/O port access can be prevented.

if (!capable(CAP_SYS_RAWIO))

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Incorrect backporting of a patch to older kernels leads to extended asm statements in the __get_user_asm_ex macro that are incompatible with the exception table.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Improper context-switching of IOPL on 64-bit PV Xen guests in the Linux kernel.

By ensuring proper handling of IOPL during context switches, unauthorized privilege escalation, denial of service attacks, and information disclosure through I/O port access can be prevented.

vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code lacks proper authorization checks based on the capabilities of the user attempting to perform socket operations, allowing unauthorized users to exploit the Netlink socket and make unauthorized network configuration changes.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to add proper authorization checks for socket operations based on the capabilities of the user. Specifically, the code should use the netlink_capable function to check for the necessary capabilities before allowing socket operations to proceed. This ensures that only authorized users with the required capabilities can perform network configuration changes using the Netlink socket.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to remove the line that sets cpuctx->ctx.type = cpu_context in the perf_pmu_register function. vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of validation to ensure that a keepalive action is associated with a stream socket, allowing local users to create a denial of service (system crash) by leveraging the ability to create a raw socket.

vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to add a condition to check if the keepalive action is associated with a stream socket and the TCP protocol before executing the action. By including the condition 'if (sk->sk_protocol == IPPROTO_TCP && sk->sk_type == SOCK_STREAM)' before setting the keepalive option, the code ensures that the keepalive action is only performed on the appropriate socket types, thereby preventing local users from causing a denial of service by creating a raw socket. This solution helps to restrict the keepalive action to the intended socket types and protocols, addressing the vulnerability.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper execute access restriction in the aio_mount function.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: Local users can bypass SELinux W^X policy restrictions and gain privileges via an io_setup system call due to the lack of execute access restriction.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code in the aio_mount function does not properly restrict execute access, making it easier for local users to bypass SELinux W^X policy restrictions and escalate privileges.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to enforce proper execute access restrictions in the aio_mount function by setting the SB_I_NOEXEC flag on the superblock of the mounted filesystem. This ensures that the filesystem is mounted with the noexec flag, preventing local users from bypassing SELinux W^X policy restrictions and gaining unauthorized privileges via the io_setup system call.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper consideration for namespaces being inapplicable to inodes in the Linux kernel before version 3.14.8.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: Local users creating a user namespace and setting the setgid bit on a file with group ownership of root.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code uses the vulnerable function inode_capable, which does not properly handle capabilities with respect to inode UID and GID due to the lack of consideration for namespaces being inapplicable to inodes.

non_vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to replace the call to inode_capable with the function capable_wrt_inode_uidgid. This updated code properly handles capabilities with respect to the inode's UID and GID, ensuring that the intended chmod restrictions are enforced correctly and preventing local users from bypassing security restrictions.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper restriction on changes to the MNT_READONLY flag in the clone_mnt function.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: Local users leveraging a separate mount namespace can bypass the intended read-only property of a filesystem.

vulnerability_behavior.preconditions_for_vulnerability: Lack of proper handling for the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.
vulnerability_behavior.trigger_condition: When unsharing a user namespace, the code does not set the CLONE_FS flag along with the CLONE_NEWUSER flag, leading to a vulnerability.
vulnerability_behavior.specific_code_behavior_causing_vulnerabi: The code does not include the CLONE_FS flag when unsharing a user namespace, allowing local users to gain privileges by calling chroot and exploiting the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes.

non_vul_knowledge.solution_behavior: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to ensure that when unsharing a user namespace (CLONE_NEWUSER flag is set), both the CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_FS flags are also set. This prevents local users from gaining privileges by leveraging the sharing of the / directory between parent and child processes. The solution involves adding the line 'unshare_flags |= CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_FS;' to properly handle the combination of CLONE_NEWUSER and CLONE_FS flags during the unshare system call.

solution_behavior.description: To mitigate the vulnerability, it is necessary to remove the vulnerable code handling F_GETLK64, F_SETLK64, and F_SETLKW64 commands in the fcntl64 system call. Instead, directly call a secure function for these commands.
